text: Thirteen point eight billion years ago, space began to expand, and filled with hydrogen and helium.
Three hundred and eighty thousand years later, the first light broke free.
We still see that light today, more sharply with every telescope.
After a hundred million years of darkness, the first stars began to shine.
They were giants. They lived fast and exploded, forging carbon, oxygen and iron.
Every heavy atom on Earth was made this way.
Over billions of years, spinning gas settled into disks. Ours, the Milky Way, began very early.
Today it holds a hundred to four hundred billion stars.
Four and a half billion years ago, a cloud collapsed, and the Sun lit up.
A Mars-sized world struck the young Earth. The debris became our Moon.
The young Earth was lava, steam and impacts, with no oxygen in the air.
Then microbes learned to use sunlight, and filled the air with oxygen.
Oxygen built the ozone layer, and the sky gained its layers.
Continents gathered and broke apart, again and again.
Rodinia.
Gondwana.
Pangaea.
Sixty-six million years ago, an asteroid ended the age of the dinosaurs.
And three hundred thousand years ago, the first people arrived.
Six phases. Thirteen point eight billion years.
